directions.description: Replace the tested axiom with Balthasar's independence-of-nilpotent-parameters / silent-coordinate condition (compatibility with setting subsets of t_j=0); test candidate (a) and the full family {Phi^(b,c)} against it, simultaneously resolving Melchior's free routing constant c.
directions.routes_around: Balthasar vacuous-or-trivial + Casper informational concurrence (wrong symmetry group chosen, S_2 relabeling structurally cannot discriminate) AND Melchior gap-found (candidate (b) underspecified by a free constant c)
directions.heuristic: Balthasar's own partial sketch already shows (a) passes unconditionally and (b) only at c=0 under t_2=0; full formalization across all c and general coupled F is unconfirmed.

directions.description: Drop symmetry/naturality framing entirely; reformulate the hypothesis as a direct information-preservation condition on the routing map rho (e.g. injectivity on the other-index derivative slot / explicit quantification of cross-derivative data discarded), making 'how much cross-index data survives' the literal subject instead of a symmetry proxy for it.
directions.routes_around: Casper's named failure mode: a symmetry group can be structurally too coarse for the axis actually in dispute; this direction uses no symmetry group at all for the load-bearing hypothesis
directions.heuristic: Closer to what per-coordinate extension needs (faithful transport of coupling information) than any relabeling symmetry; satisfiability by any map into the 2-dimensional codomain is unconfirmed.

directions.description: Revive r2-propose's unused Direction 2 (construct, don't test, the routing map via symmetrization/coinvariant descent) but descend under the independent per-coordinate scaling group (R^x)^n instead of the S_n relabeling group now shown structurally non-discriminating.
directions.routes_around: Round 2's structural finding that S_n-descent targets the wrong invariant (every own-vs-other-index rule already descends trivially under relabeling)
directions.heuristic: Averaging/coinvariant construction under a continuous scaling group rather than a finite permutation group is a different, less standard tool; whether a nonzero well-typed canonical map results is unconfirmed.

directions.description: Import the KMS-style two-Weil-algebra base/fiber bundle functor T^{A,B} to supply cross-term compatibility by construction, carried forward untouched from Round 1's propose Direction C, in place of any hand-built routing map plus after-the-fact symmetry test.
directions.routes_around: The whole family of problems Round 1 and Round 2 exposed (underspecified ad hoc routing maps; symmetry axioms that don't bite) by not constructing a routing map from scratch at all
directions.heuristic: Unconfirmed whether T^{A,B}'s one base/one fiber compatibility shape can express the n-coordinate per-coordinate setup without collapsing back to a two-algebra picture; a lead, not a settled applicability result.
